title: Mohammed the Dandy and the Test of True Loyalty

keywords: mohammed the shalabi and his mistress and his wife
full_text:
Mohammed the Shalabi (The Fashionable Youth) was the darling of Cairo's elite salons. Wealthy, handsome, and foolishly vain, he spent his patrimony hosting lavish feasts for shallow acquaintances and shower gifts on glamorous flatterers, while neglecting his prudent, modest wife, Fatima, who kept their ancestral home in quiet order.

One day, his wise father-in-law, Sheikh Hasan, resolved to open Mohammed's eyes to the superficiality of his companions.
Sheikh Hasan instructed Mohammed to test his companions:
'Kill a sheep from the flock, sew it inside a blood-stained linen shroud, carry it to the doors of thy fashionable friends at midnight, and tell them thou hast killed a man in an accidental brawl and need a secret garden to bury the corpse.'

Mohammed laughed, confident in his friends' devotion.
At midnight, he dragged the blood-stained bundle to the mansion of his closest dining companion, Emir Basim.
When Basim heard the plea, he slammed the door shut from the inside, whispering: 'Madman! Dost thou wish to hang me with thee? Away from my gate!'
He went to the second friend, a poet who had composed twenty odes to their eternal friendship. The poet threatened to call the night watch if Mohammed did not vanish immediately!
A third fashionable companion refused even to unlatch his shutters.

Shattered and exhausted, Mohammed returned to his own home at dawn, dragging the heavy sack.
Fatima met him at the courtyard gate. Seeing the blood-stained sack and Mohammed's trembling hands, she did not scold, panic, or ask questions.
She locked the outer gate, brought a shovel from the garden shed, and said with quiet tears:
'Husband, whatever misfortune has befallen thee, thy life is my life. Let us bury it beneath the fig tree, and if the watch comes, I will stand beside thee to the end.'

Mohammed dropped the sack, unstitched the linen, and revealed the sheep's carcass!
He fell to his knees before Fatima, weeping in profound shame:
'My noble wife! I squandered fortunes on wolves who fled at the first shadow of danger, while ignoring the angel who stood ready to share my grave!'

Mohammed renounced his frivolous lifestyle forever. He dedicated his life to Fatima and their family, living in honor and mutual devotion, having learned that true loyalty is found not in festive laughter, but in the steadfast courage of love.
moral: Flattery and fair-weather friends vanish in the hour of trial; genuine fidelity is proven by quiet sacrifice.
